articles.title: The AI-Driven Memory Shortage: DRAM Prices, Inflation and Market Risks
articles.dek: The latest bottleneck in AI expansion is memory chip and DRAM storage, with knock-on effects in inflation and national security.
points: AI data center construction and hyperscaler demand are absorbing a disproportionate share of global memory capacity, creating a dynamic random access memory (DRAM) shortage that may take years to unwind.
J.P. Morgan Global Research estimates that DRAM prices will have risen more than 400% from the start of 2024 to the end of 2026.
The Consumer Price Index (CPI) for software and accessories and Producer Price Index (PPI) for storage devices have both risen 23% since the end of 2024.

The memory supply crunch is also straining cybersecurity infrastructure, with analysts warning that a major cyberattack could unleash an estimated $145 billion in additional chip demand on an already constrained market.

articles.title: On the ball: World Cup 2026 final score
articles.dek: The FIFA World Cup 2026™ delivered a clear spending boost to US host cities, led by traveling fans.
points: The FIFA World Cup 2026™ boosted local spending, led by traveling fans, according to Bank of America credit and debit card data. Over the tournament, card spending in host cities rose around 5% year-over-year (YoY), with the strongest gains coming from non-locals, whose spending was up more than 17% YoY. Restaurants and bars were the clearest beneficiaries as fans splashed out on hospitality.

Kansas City got the golden boot, recording a 7% rise in card spending. But gains were broadly shared across host cities, with Philadelphia, Los Angeles, Miami and New York/New Jersey also enjoying substantial boosts. Host cities generally experienced stronger growth in restaurant and bar spending than non-host cities, particularly during the knockout stages.

articles.title: What’s The Fed’s Next Move?
articles.dek: J.P. Morgan Global Research now sees the Fed hiking rates in December, especially as the central bank has yet to lay out a roadmap for tackling inflation.
points: The Federal Reserve (Fed) held rates at 3.5–3.75% in July despite growing inflation concerns, leaving its path forward unclear.
J.P. Morgan Global Research now expects the first hike of 25 basis points (bp) to take place in December, with policy rates holding at 3.75–4.0% thereafter.
The five new Fed task forces are slated to deliver their findings by year-end, but this is unlikely to have a significant bearing on the near-term policy outlook.

articles.title: The Institute Employment Report: July 2026
articles.dek: Lower-income households are seeing stronger job and after-tax wage growth in Bank of America data.
points: Bank of America customer deposit account data suggests labor market momentum strengthened further in July, with estimated payroll growth accelerating to 2.0% year-over-year (YoY), up from 1.7% in June.
Job growth was led by lower-income households, while unemployment payments into customer accounts remained subdued, pointing to continued labor market resilience.

Lower-income households saw after-tax wage growth accelerate to 5.2% YoY in July, surpassing higher-income households for the first time since December 2024, potentially aided by increased job switching and lower tax withholdings. Still, despite the strength in "regular" employment, the share of workers supplementing their income with gig work was up 0.4 percentage points YoY in June.

articles.title: ETF Market Guide: Understanding the $22 Trillion Industry
articles.dek: ETFs continue to grow in scale and complexity, with total assets under management up 43% year over year as of April 2026. What are their benefits, and how are regional ETF markets performing?
points: ETFs offer investors various benefits, including portfolio diversification, intraday liquidity and lower costs compared with mutual funds.
Total ETF assets under management (AUM) amounted to around $22.1 trillion globally as of end-April 2026.
Active ETF products continue to scale rapidly, representing more than 60% of new launches in each of the past six years.

articles.title: US Tariffs: What’s the Impact?
articles.dek: The situation surrounding U.S. tariffs is constantly evolving. Read the latest analysis of their economic impact from J.P. Morgan Global Research.
points: President Trump has floated tariffs on imported generic medicines in a bid to move production to the U.S. Under this proposal, which has not been finalized, generic drugs would initially not face any tariffs for two years starting from August 1, 2026, after which rates will be raised to 100% for one year (from August 2028) and to 200% thereafter.
July 20: The Trump administration announces 50% tariffs on Canadian imports
June 7: The US lowers tariffs on agricultural and industrial equipment

“The move, in theory, encourages foreign companies to use more U.S. steel and aluminum, which could drive incremental exports, while also supporting farmers, construction, logistics and manufacturers that rely on equipment currently treated as steel or aluminum derivatives,” said Bill Peterson, senior analyst for Metals & Mining at J.P. Morgan.

articles.title: Oil Prices Forecast
articles.dek: Surprising movements in supply and demand have complicated the outlook for oil prices.
points: J.P. Morgan Global Research now forecasts Brent crude to average $86 per barrel (bbl) in the third quarter of 2026, $80 in the fourth quarter and $78 at year end.
The oil market has rebalanced via larger-than-expected demand losses and smaller-than-expected OECD commercial inventory draws, with China providing a case study in possible demand destruction.
Long-term damage to oil production in the Gulf region is believed to be minimal, though the uncertain future of OPEC may complicate oil price predictions.

articles.title: 2026 Mid-Year Market Outlook
articles.dek: While the global expansion stands on solid ground, markets will need to balance competing forces as they head into the second half of the year.
points: Global growth is supported by improving business sentiment, a resilient consumer and a surge in AI-driven capital spending, despite the oil supply shock.
J.P. Morgan Global Research is constructive on equities and has increased its S&P 500 year-end price target to 7,800.
Elsewhere, it is bullish on the dollar and has revised its oil price framework, with Brent now likely exiting the year at $78 per barrel (bbl).

articles.title: 2026 Mid-Year Investment Outlook
articles.dek: Explore our Mid-Year Investment Outlook for 2026 and see our forecasts and potential investment opportunities amidst the evolving economic and market landscapes.
points: Economic momentum has increased in 2026 as the investment boom from the AI surge and consumption gains from wealth effects and big income tax refunds have more than offset the negative effects of Iran War uncertainty and higher energy prices.

CPI inflation hit a three-year high of 4.2% in May. However, it could drift down slowly from that level over the rest of 2026, provided there is a durable resolution to the Strait of Hormuz crisis, reflecting lower energy inflation, lower tariffs, lower shelter inflation and only moderate wage growth.
We expect the Fed to remain on hold for the rest of this year but could ease modestly in 2027, causing the dollar exchange rate to renew its decline.

Bonds are now priced for inflation and Fed rate hikes, with the short end of the yield curve offering a meaningful yield pick-up versus cash. While the Fed is on pause, the income across fixed income is not – and it is supported by solid municipal, corporate and household balance sheets.
